name: 180. Catalog routing: a model named without a provider (catalog-routing)
description:
Wire-level pins for the model catalog resolver, which picks a provider for a model named without one. Each row creates two run-scoped OpenAI-backed providers whose keys serve the row's own model, an alias of gpt-4o-mini, so the catalog finds exactly those two. Provider a sorts first by name and holds a dead key OpenAI refuses for free; provider b holds a live key.

Rows: (1) the catalog sends the model to provider a, the first candidate in name order, and attaches provider b as a fallback, which serves; the log row records both candidates, the pick and the fallback; (2) a caller's own fallbacks replace the catalog's, so provider b is never tried; (3) the same while streaming; (4) a /v1/responses request; (5) the /anthropic route, where Anthropic is not a candidate; (6) a virtual key that allows only provider b sends the request there directly, with governance choosing before the catalog runs; (7) a model no provider serves is refused with 400, asking the caller to name a provider. (8) a session whose first turn the catalog fallback b served starts its next turns on b, ahead of the catalog's first candidate a, with the trail naming the session. Each row deletes what it made. Row 1 also keeps a virtual key weighing b over a that its requests do not carry, and once a's key works the catalog's pick serves twenty requests itself. Run with FEATURE="catalog-routing".
